'''''1492: Conquest of Paradise''''' is a 1992 [[Epic film|epic]] [[Historical film|historical]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama film]] directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and written by [[Roselyne Bosch]]. It stars [[Gérard Depardieu]], [[Armand Assante]], and [[Sigourney Weaver]], and portrays the travels to the [[New World]] by the Spanish explorer [[Christopher Columbus]] and the effect this had on [[indigenous peoples of the Americas|Indigenous peoples]].

The film was released to celebrate the [[Columbus Quincentenary|500th anniversary]] of Columbus's voyage. It debuted less than two months after [[John Glen (director)|John Glen]]'s film ''[[Christopher Columbus: The Discovery]]'', often leading to confusion between the two. The film received mixed to negative reviews, with particular criticism aimed at its historical inaccuracy and dramatic quality, and was commercially unsuccessful in the United States, doing better at the box office in Europe.

==Plot==
{{See also|Voyages of Christopher Columbus}}
Aware that the {{nowrap|world{{px2}}{{mdash}}{{px2}}}}‌covered mostly in apparently flat {{nowrap|ocean{{px2}}{{mdash}}{{px2}}}}‌actually has a ball-shaped surface, [[Christopher Columbus]] lobbies for a trip westward to Asia, but lacks a crew and ship. The Catholic theologians at the [[University of Salamanca]] heavily disapprove of Columbus's plan, not being keen on ideas that go against the writings of [[Ptolemaeus]]. Columbus is approached by [[Martín Pinzón]], a shipowner from [[Palos de la Frontera|Palos]], who introduces him to the banker [[Luis de Santángel|Santángel]], to whom [[Queen Isabella I]] owes money. Columbus meets with the queen, who grants him his journey in exchange for his promise to bring back sufficient amounts of riches in gold.

Columbus deceives many crewmen by telling them that the voyage will only last seven weeks. Three ships pass. Nine weeks go by with no sign of land. The crew becomes restless and edges toward [[mutiny]]. He tries to reinvigorate them with an inspiring speech, coinciding with a fast wind, which goads the men to return to their duties. At night, Columbus notices mosquitoes on the deck, indicating that land is not far off. Suddenly, out of the mist they see the lush vegetation and sandy beaches of [[Guanahani]].

The Europeans befriend the local natives, who show them gold they have collected. Columbus teaches one of them Spanish so that they are able to communicate. He then informs them that he will return to Spain, which will be followed by the arrival of many more Europeans. Columbus leaves behind a group to begin the [[colonisation of the Americas]]. Back in Spain, he receives a high honour from the queen and has dinner with the council. They express disappointment with the small amount of gold he brought back, but the queen approves of his gifts. On the second expedition, Columbus takes 17 ships and over 1,000 men with him to the island; however, all the crewmen left behind are found to have been killed. When the tribe is confronted by Columbus and his troops, they tell him that another tribe came and killed them. Columbus chooses to believe them, but his arrogant aristocratic subordinate [[Adrián de Moxica|Moxica]] is not convinced. They begin to build the city of [[La Isabela]] and eventually manage to hoist the town bell into its tower.

Four years later, the natives are being forced to mine for gold. Moxica punishes one who fails to find any gold by cutting off his hand. The word of this act of violence spreads throughout the native tribes and they all disappear into the forest. Columbus begins to worry about a potential war, with the natives heavily outnumbering them. Upon return to his home, he finds his house set ablaze by Moxica and his followers, confirming his unpopularity among a certain faction of the settlers. Soon, the tribes arrive to fight the Spaniards and the island becomes war-torn. The settlers fight among themselves; Columbus' faction eventually prevails over Moxica's. Rather than be captured, Moxica commits suicide. Columbus' governorship is reassigned with orders for him to return to Spain.

Columbus is accused of [[nepotism]] and offering administrative positions to his personal friends, thereby injuring the pride of the nobles such as Moxica; he is replaced by [[Francisco de Bobadilla|de Bobadilla]]. Columbus returns to [[Castile (historical region)|Castile]] to be imprisoned, but is [[bail]]ed out by his sons. When he is summoned by the queen, she is reluctantly convinced to allow him to make another voyage, with the proviso that he neither take his brothers nor return to the colonies. As an old man, Columbus is virtually forgotten in Spain, with the discovery of the [[New World]] being credited to [[Amerigo Vespucci]]. Columbus's son [[Ferdinand Columbus|Ferdinand]] asks his father to tell him his story so he can transcribe it.
==Production==
Principal photography ran from December 1991 to March 1992. The New World sequences were shot on the central Pacific coast of Costa Rica, in [[Puntarenas Province]]: Columbus's landfall and the settlement of [[La Isabela]] were staged on the beaches around Playa Herradura, Punta Leona and [[Jacó]], where roughly ten sets were built.<ref name="ticotimes2024">{{Cite news |date=9 April 2024 |title=Costa Rica Chosen As Filming Location for Upcoming Hallmark Channel Movie |newspaper=[[The Tico Times]] |url=https://ticotimes.net/2024/04/09/costa-rica-chosen-as-filming-location-for-upcoming-hallmark-channel-movie |access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="movieloc">{{Cite web |title=Filming Locations for 1492: Conquest of Paradise (1992) |url=https://movie-locations.com/movies/0/1492-Conquest-Of-Paradise.php |website=movie-locations.com |access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref> The production hired about 170 Indigenous Costa Ricans as extras to portray the Caribbean islanders, paying around $35 a day; a newly formed national film commission helped secure the country as a location.<ref name="ticotimes2006">{{Cite news |date=12 May 2006 |title=Costa Rica: Hollywood South? |newspaper=[[The Tico Times]] |url=https://ticotimes.net/2006/05/12/costa-rica-hollywood-south |access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref> Other locations included the Dominican Republic, the [[United States Virgin Islands|U.S. Virgin Islands]], Spain ([[Cáceres, Spain|Cáceres]], [[Trujillo, Cáceres|Trujillo]], [[Seville]] and [[Salamanca]]) and [[Pinewood Studios]] in England.

==Music==
{{Main|1492: Conquest of Paradise (album)}}{{More citations needed section|date=September 2026}}
The Greek composer [[Vangelis]], who previously worked for Ridley Scott on ''[[Blade Runner]]'' (1982), composed the score. Its main theme, "[[Conquest of Paradise (song)|Conquest of Paradise]]", was used by former [[List of Prime Ministers of Portugal|Portuguese Prime Minister]] [[António Guterres]] at his [[1995 Portuguese legislative election|1995 election]] and it was used by the [[Socialist Party (Portugal)|Portuguese Socialist Party]] as its campaign and rally anthem,<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 January 2005 |title=Hinos, campanhas e conquistadores |url=https://www.publico.pt/2005/01/24/jornal/hinos-campanhas-e-conquistadores-1950 |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Publico}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pereira |first=Helena |date=June 4, 2016 |title=Congresso do PS aplaude de pé Guterres com Vangelis |url=https://expresso.pt/nosection/foruns/forum_politica/2016-06-04-Congresso-do-PS-aplaude-de-pe-Guterres-com-Vangelis |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516225815/https://expresso.pt/nosection/foruns/forum_politica/2016-06-04-Congresso-do-PS-aplaude-de-pe-Guterres-com-Vangelis |archive-date=2024-05-16 |access-date=2026-09-11 |work=Jornal Expresso |language=pt-PT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tavares |first=Rita |date=September 26, 2019 |title=Costa ao som de Vangelis a diabolizar regresso do PSD/CDS para espantar as sondagens |url=https://observador.pt/2019/09/26/costa-ao-som-de-vangelis-a-diabolizar-regresso-do-psd-cds-a-tentar-espantar-as-sondagens/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Observador |language=pt-PT}}</ref> although it was replaced by the main theme from ''[[Gladiator (2000 film)|Gladiator]]'' (2000), another Scott film, since the first José Sócrates legislative elections campaign.<ref>[http://a-espera-de-godot.blogspot.pt/2011/09/bandas-sonoras.html Bandas Sonoras], blog ''À Espera de Godot'', 13 September 2011 (Portuguese)</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable because it is a blog.|date=September 2026}} Despite the film's dismal box office intake in the United States, the film's score became a successful album worldwide.

Russia used it in the 2nd round of the [[1996 Russian presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=КАШИН |url=https://t.me/kashinguru/36151 |website=Telegram}}</ref>{{Clarify|date=August 2022}}{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable because it is user generated.|date=September 2026}}

The theme is also used at the starting line of the ''[[Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc]]'' ultramarathon. German boxer [[Henry Maske]], the [[IBF]] [[light heavyweight]] world champion from 1993 to 1996, used the theme as his entrance music, which helped make it a hit in Germany.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Spahr |first=Wolfgang |date=January 20, 1996 |title=Sporting Events and Personalities Giving a Big Boost to Record Sales for Labels |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3g4EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA41&dq=%22When+the+Vangelis+song+%22Conquest+Of+Paradise%22+was+telecast+to+an+audience%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwj3zv2jh-aWAxUMD1kFHVUjOtsQ6AF6BAgJEAM#v=onepage&q&f=false |access-date=September 11, 2026 |magazine=Billboard |page=41 |via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Henry Maske |website=Hall of Fame des deutschen Sports |language=de |url=https://www.hall-of-fame-sport.de/mitglieder/detail/Henry-Maske |access-date=2026-09-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Vangelis ist gestorben |website=FAZEmag |language=de |url=https://www.fazemag.de/vangelis-ist-gestorben/ |access-date=2026-09-29}}</ref>

Other usages of the theme include New Zealand [[Super Rugby|Super 15 Rugby]] franchise the [[Canterbury Crusaders]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ewing |first=Jerry |date=2025-06-25 |title=Vangelis's epic 1492: Conquest Of Paradise soundtrack to be reissued on coloured vinyl and CD |url=https://www.loudersound.com/bands-artists/vangeliss-epic-1492-conquest-of-paradise-soundtrack-to-be-reissued-on-coloured-vinyl-and-cd |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Louder |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 13, 2026 |title=Crusaders' match-day horses put out to pasture |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/crusaders-match-day-horses-put-out-pasture-2026-04-14/ |access-date=September 11, 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref> as they run onto the field, often accompanied by actors dressed as knights and riding on horseback, the Northampton Saints rugby team for their entrance into the Franklins Gardens stadium and [[rugby league]] team [[Wigan Warriors]] who play in the [[Super League]], as well as being played before the start of every match in the 2010 and 2014 cricket [[ICC World Twenty20|World Twenty20]] championships as well as the [[2011 ICC Cricket World Cup|2011 Cricket World Cup]]. In these events the theme was played right before the national anthems of the two competing nations, as the flags of the two nations were carried into the ground, accompanied by the players of the two teams.

The theme was also played in the ''[[Top Gear: US Special]]'' and became a signature piece for World Professional Champion figure skaters Anita Hartshorn and Frank Sweiding.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stevens |first=Ryan |date=June 1, 2013 |title=Interview With Anita Hartshorn |url=https://www.skateguardblog.com/2013/06/interview-with-anita-hartshorn.html |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Skate Guard Blog |language=en}}</ref> In Lebanon it has been used almost at every wedding since its release until now, mostly used as starter music before the arrival of the bride and the groom.

==Reception==
===Box office===
''1492: Conquest of Paradise'' opened on 66 screens in Spain, grossing $1{{spaces}}million in its first five days<ref name=open/> (${{Inflation|US|1|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today).{{Inflation-fn|US}} In the United States and Canada, it was released by [[Paramount Pictures]] on 9{{spaces}}October 1992 in 1,008 theaters. The version released there was edited to 150{{spaces}}minutes, with some violence and brutality removed in order to achieve a PG-13 rating.<ref>{{AFI film|59248}}</ref> The film was a [[Box-office bomb|flop]] in the United States, debuting at number seven with a gross of $3,002,680 (about ${{Inflation|US|3.003|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today),{{Inflation-fn|US}} worse than the opening of ''[[Christopher Columbus: The Discovery]]'' earlier in the year, and went on to gross just $7{{spaces}}million<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Cohn |first=Lawrence |date=19 October 1992 |title=National B.O. |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |page=10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fox |first=David J. |date=13 October 1992 |title=Weekend Box Office A Bang-Up Opening for 'Under Siege' |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-10-13-ca-32-story.html |access-date=1 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Mojo title|1492}}</ref> (${{Inflation|US|7|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today).{{Inflation-fn|US}} It opened in France on 12{{spaces}}October 1992, grossing $1.46{{spaces}}million for the weekend (${{Inflation|US|1.46|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today){{Inflation-fn|US}} from 264{{spaces}}screens.<ref name="open">{{Cite magazine |last=Groves |first=Don |date=19 October 1992 |title=Smooth sailing for '1492' in debuts |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |page=60}}</ref> In its second week in Europe, it was the highest-grossing film with a gross of over $7.7{{spaces}}million (${{Inflation|US|7.7|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today),{{Inflation-fn|US}} including $1.77{{spaces}}million in its opening week in Germany (${{Inflation|US|1.77|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today){{Inflation-fn|US}} from 213{{spaces}}screens. It did not open well in Italy, with only $261,800 in its opening weekend (${{Inflation|US|261800|1992|r=-2|fmt=c}}{{spaces}} today){{Inflation-fn|US}} from 33{{spaces}}screens.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=26 October 1992 |title=Top 10 Europe's Big Pics |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |page=31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Groves |first=Don |date=26 October 1992 |title=Italians snub their local hero at B.O. |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |page=40}}</ref> By the end of 1992, it had grossed $40{{spaces}}million internationally (${{Inflation|US|40|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today),{{Inflation-fn|US}}, including $17 million in France and €3 million in Spain,<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=26 March 1993|page=34|title=Statistics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=1492: LA CONQUISTA DEL PARAISO|url=https://sede.mcu.gob.es/CatalogoICAA/Peliculas/Detalle?Pelicula=102291|website=The Spanish Film Catalogue|access-date=January 14, 2024}}</ref> for a worldwide total of $47{{spaces}}million<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=4 January 1993 |title=U.S. pics at home and abroad |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |page=56}}</ref> (${{Inflation|US|47|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today).{{Inflation-fn|US}} It went on to gross $59{{spaces}}million (${{Inflation|US|59|1992|r=1}}{{spaces}}million today).{{Inflation-fn|US}}

Scott later blamed the film's U.S. failure on Americans not understanding European accents: "They don't hear shit unless it's from Texas or America, right?" and reflected: "It's one of my favorite films. What's interesting, they didn't know how to release it in America. But in Europe, it clocked $57 million."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/ridley-scott-interview-house-of-gucci-dune/|title = Ridley Scott interview on House of Gucci, Lady Gaga, and dropping out of Dune|date = 26 November 2021|website=GamesRadar|last=Shepherd|first=Jack}}</ref> In 2024, he give a similar statement: "I'm very proud of ''1492'', with Gérard Depardieu. The problem with Gérard is he doesn't speak very good English and I didn't have the heart to say, 'Gérard we need to [re-record all your lines].' I'm trying to resurrect ''1492'' because it's so beautifully shot and acted and scored. I'm trying to resurrect it as a four-hour [movie] for a streaming platform. Now if I asked, 'Gérard, can we ADR you with Kenneth Branagh?' he'd probably say, 'Yeah, of course.{{' "}}<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/ridley-scott-interview-gladiator-2-alien-blade-runner-1236049190/ | title=Ridley Scott Will Never Stop Directing: "Shut up and Go Make Another Movie" | website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=7 November 2024 |last=Hibberd|first=James}}</ref>

===Critical response===
[[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' awarded the film three stars from four. He wrote that "Depardieu lends it gravity, the supporting performances are convincing, the locations are realistic, and we are inspired to reflect that it did indeed take a certain nerve to sail off into nowhere just because an orange was round."<ref name="ebert">{{Cite news |last=Ebert |first=Roger |date=October 9, 1992 |title=1492: Conquest Of Paradise |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/1492-conquest-of-paradise-1992 |work=Chicago Sun-Times |via=RogerEbert.com}}</ref> [[Desson Howe]] of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' said that "despite Scott's trademark, spectacular imagery, the story's dead in the water. Actually, there's no story. It's all eye-dizzying hyperbole, with astounding camerawork, fancy editing and a moody flamenco guitar-meets-synthesizer soundtrack by avant-garde musician Vangelis."<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 October 1992 |title=1492: Conquest of Paradise |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/1492conquestofparadisepg13howe_a0af13.htm |access-date=30 November 2010|last=Howe|first=Desson}}</ref> A reviewer for ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote that "Ridley Scott's vaunted visuals can't transform ''1492'' from a lumbering, one-dimensional historical fresco into the complex, ambiguous character study that it strives to be."<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 December 1991 |title=1492: Conquest of Paradise |work=Variety |url=https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117791068?refcatid=31 |url-status=live |access-date=30 November 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107043459/http://www.variety.com/review/VE1117791068?refcatid=31 |archive-date=7 November 2012}}</ref> Chris Hicks of the [[Salt Lake City]]-based ''[[Deseret News]]'' wrote that "Scott, the accomplished director of ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]'', ''[[Blade Runner]]'' and ''[[Thelma & Louise]]'', among others, has imbued this film with great visual style, and the sets, costumes and general atmosphere are fascinating. In fact, there is much to recommend on a technical level. But ''1492'' is, unfortunately, plagued with narrative problems that make it a less than successful cinematic voyage."<ref>{{Cite news |title=1492: Conquest of Paradise |work=Deseret News |url=https://www.deseret.com/1992/10/13/20086953/film-review-1492-conquest-of-paradise/ |access-date=30 November 2010|date=October 13, 1992|last=Hicks|first=Chris}}</ref> [[Owen Gleiberman]] of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' wrote that "at 2.5 hours, ''1492'' is even harder to sit through than last month’s schlock extravaganza ''[[Christopher Columbus: The Discovery]]''. In each case the filmmakers have fallen into a similar trap. Out of some vague mixture of historical 'duty' and commercial myopia, they’ve presented Columbus as the same cardboard visionary we learned about in school. Whether or not that image has a core of truth, are there really many people who want to experience it all over again at the movies? Watching ''1492'' is about as exciting as doing your homework."<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=16 October 1992 |title=1492: Conquest of Paradise |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |url=https://ew.com/article/1992/10/16/1492-conquest-paradise/ |access-date=30 November 2010|last=Gleiberman|first=Owen|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151110114257/https://ew.com/article/1992/10/16/1492-conquest-paradise/|archive-date=November 10, 2015}}</ref>

Overall, ''1492: Conquest of Paradise'' received mixed to negative reviews from critics, with the review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]] giving the film a 30% rating based on 23 reviews with the critical consensus: "Historically inaccurate and dramatically inert, Ridley Scott's retelling of Christopher Columbus' exploits is an epic without grandeur or insight".<ref>{{Cite web |title=1492: Conquest of Paradise (1992) |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1492_conquest_of_paradise |via=www.rottentomatoes.com}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 47 out of 100, based on 21 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''1492: Conquest of Paradise'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/ |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=11 September 2026 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences surveyed by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film a grade of "B+" on scale of A+ to F.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cinemascore |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220122629/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date=2018-12-20}}</ref>

The film was accused of promoting the [[Black legend (Spain)|Spanish black legend]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/cultura/2019/05/03/actualidad/1556884697_837781.html|title=La leyenda negra española que ha difundido Hollywood|first=Vicente G.|last=Olaya|newspaper=El País |date=7 May 2019|access-date=7 May 2023|via=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/historia/abci-cinco-peliculas-anglosajonas-cargadas-leyenda-negra-y-errores-historicos-sobre-espanoles-202004070146_noticia.html|title=Cinco películas anglosajonas cargadas de Leyenda Negra y errores históricos sobre los españoles|date=7 April 2020|website=ABC|access-date=7 May 2023|last=Cervera|first=César}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/la-lectura/2022/09/09/631a3234fc6c83d7778b45c9.html|title=Cine y Leyenda Negra: España en el banquillo|date=9 September 2022|website=ELMUNDO|access-date=7 May 2023|last=Pena|first=Guzman Urrero}}</ref>
